title: Get Paid Every Month Without Selling a Share
creator: BWB - Business With Brian
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garble some names and figures in places
summary: Brian opens by noting dividend names are beating tech in 2026: Coca-Cola is up about 40% including dividends while Nvidia is down about 4%. The catch is that KO and SCHD pay only quarterly, so he hunts for monthly payers that still grow, applying a price test: a fund's price must be higher than five years ago or than at launch. He explains three dividend mistakes through quizzes: misreading an annual yield as a monthly one, the dividend trap (a 15% yield with a 5% total return loses to a 5% yield with an 8% total return), and qualified versus non-qualified dividend tax. He argues these funds belong in an IRA: $100,000 at 8% grows to about $1.1 million over 30 years tax-deferred versus roughly $650,000 taxable. His six BUYs are JEPQ (about 12% yield; 3-year total return about 74% versus about 100% for the Nasdaq), DIVO (about 5%; fell less than the S&P 500 in every big drop), SPYI (about 12%; barely passed the price test), IDVO (about 6%; up 81% over three years, best of the five), DHS (about 3%; $10,000 became about $18,000 over five years) and Main Street Capital (about 6%; never cut its monthly dividend since 2007, but fell about 64% in the 2020 crash, so keep it small). JEPI, QYLD and Realty Income (O) are AVOIDs for failing the price test. For $5,000 a month he says $500,000 is needed in JEPQ or SPYI, $1.2 million in DIVO and $1.9 million in DHS.

calls.video_title: Get Paid Every Month Without Selling a Share
calls.thesis: First pick on his monthly-dividend list: JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income ETF, holds NVDA/AAPL/MSFT and sells covered calls for income.
calls.base_case: Tech exposure plus a ~12% annual yield paid monthly.
calls.bull_case: Monthly checks keep coming even in drawdowns; dividend stocks fell less than Nasdaq in past drops.
calls.bear_case: Selling options caps upside in big rallies (74% vs Nasdaq 100% over 3 yrs); distributions mostly non-qualified (taxed as income).

calls.video_title: Get Paid Every Month Without Selling a Share
calls.thesis: Amplify CWP Enhanced Dividend Income ETF: ~30 big dividend payers (MSFT, VISA, CAT), sells options only on some stocks some of the time.
calls.base_case: Steadier price with a smaller check; fell less than the S&P 500 in every big market drop he cites.
calls.bull_case: Best pick for someone living off the checks who worries about a bad year.
calls.bear_case: Lower yield than the option-heavy funds; still gives up some upside when it sells calls.

calls.video_title: Get Paid Every Month Without Selling a Share
calls.thesis: NEOS S&P 500 High Income ETF: owns the whole S&P 500, sells options; most payouts labelled return of capital.
calls.base_case: Big monthly check from the whole S&P 500, not just tech.
calls.bear_case: Barely passed his price test (price only ~8% above launch); return-of-capital payouts.

calls.video_title: Get Paid Every Month Without Selling a Share
calls.price_at_call: ~6% yield/yr; +81% total return over 3 yrs through Oct
calls.thesis: Amplify CWP International Enhanced Dividend Income ETF: dividend payers outside the US (TSM, big Japanese/Canadian banks).
calls.base_case: Best 3-yr total return of the five ETFs (+81% incl. dividends).
calls.bull_case: Diversifies dividend income away from the S&P 500.
calls.bear_case: Only ~4 years old, untested in a full bear market (-20% or more).

calls.video_title: Get Paid Every Month Without Selling a Share
calls.thesis: WisdomTree US High Dividend Fund: 300+ steady dividend payers (ABBV, XOM, PM); no MSFT/AAPL near the top.
calls.base_case: Monthly checks from established companies, beat the S&P 500 over 5 years.
calls.bull_case: Five-year total return beat the S&P 500.
calls.bear_case: Fell ~37% in the 2020 COVID crash, slightly more than the S&P 500.

calls.video_title: Get Paid Every Month Without Selling a Share
calls.thesis: Main Street Capital: lends to smaller private companies, never cut its regular monthly dividend since 2007; the only monthly dividend stock that made his list, keep it small.
calls.base_case: Never cut its regular monthly dividend since 2007; 5-yr total return beat the S&P.
calls.bull_case: Reliable monthly payer with a long no-cut record.
calls.bear_case: Sold first when investors fear private lending; fell ~64% in the 2020 COVID crash.

calls.video_title: Get Paid Every Month Without Selling a Share
calls.thesis: Excluded from his list: the older JPMorgan covered-call ETF failed his price test (price lower than 5 years ago / at launch).
calls.base_case: Failed the price test, so a monthly check that still loses money on price.
calls.bear_case: Price erosion means the yield does not compensate.

calls.base_case: Failed the price test, so a monthly check that still loses money on price.

calls.video_title: Get Paid Every Month Without Selling a Share
calls.price_at_call: No stated price; price down ~14% over 5 yrs

calls.bear_case: Monthly dividend does not offset a shrinking share price.
